failure1and2_dataSurface.symptom: missingHooks(readMarkupForScan()) returned ['data-surface'] at src/addressability.test.mjs:918, plus the companion firing arm, for the same cause.
failure1and2_dataSurface.rootCause: G-89 added html[data-surface] .lens and fifteen html[data-surface="lens-x"] #lens-x rules to web/shell.css, so data-surface correctly entered HOOKS_BY_CSS. It is stamped at runtime and is legitimately absent from static markup. My HOOKS_WRITTEN derived only from `X.dataset.Y =`; the sibling writes through root.setAttribute("data-surface", ...). The instrument was RIGHT and its derivation was SHORT.
failure1and2_dataSurface.theHalfIWouldHaveMissed: data-tab and data-atab are written the same way and escaped the same false positive only because they also happen to sit in static markup on the tab anchors. Two of three passing by luck is not two of three passing. The planner caught that and it changed the fix.
failure1and2_dataSurface.fix1_bothWriteForms: hooksWrittenByScripts now derives from BOTH write forms: `X.dataset.Y =` and setAttribute("data-...", ...), the latter tolerant of the multi-line call shape the head script uses. Derived and recomputed every run; no hardcoded data-surface entry, which would have been the has_writer defect CP1 refused.
failure1and2_dataSurface.fix2_inlineScripts: Inline <script> blocks now JOIN the script population and their bodies LEAVE the markup population. G-89's first-paint stamp is a classless inline script in the head of web/index.html - deliberately not in app.js, because a type=module script is deferred by definition and can never run before first paint - so the EARLIEST writer of a behaviour hook in this product lives inside a markup file, and a served-files-only derivation cannot see it. The markup direction matters too: an attribute NAME inside a string literal is not an attached attribute, and today only the quote character in front of "data-surface" kept it out of the attached set. Depending on a quote is not a rule. Verified a NO-OP on all three attached scans before landing: 94 ids, the same 15 attached hooks, 14 hidden branches, with and without the strip.
failure1and2_dataSurface.fix3_subtractionNarrowerThanInstructed: Subtracting every script-written hook would have been wrong in the other direction, and this is the one place I did not follow the brief literally. data-tab and data-atab are stamped on <html> AND attached to the tab anchors, where `.tabs [data-tab]` reads them off descendants: one attribute name, two element populations. A global name-level exclusion would have silently dropped six tab anchors out of coverage in order to fix one false positive. So a hook is excused only when a script provably writes it AND it is attached nowhere in static markup. Both halves are required - the second alone would be 'excuse whatever is missing', which is the gate agreeing with the defect.
failure1and2_dataSurface.residualHazardPinned: That derivation reads what is attached TODAY, so if a translation ever dropped data-tab from every anchor it would move from required to excused and go quiet. The excused set is therefore PINNED, which is the one place a pin is right: it is the exclusion set, where DEV_PROCESS 2.1 says the contract belongs, and it fails on membership change in either direction.

A pin that re-arms whenever anyone writes a comment containing a dotted filename is a gate that only ever goes red for non-defects - the DEV_PROCESS 2.0 shape, where a gate nobody can keep green stops being read. failure3_commentOnlyPin.whatIsAssertedNow: Three things, all load-bearing and none of which grows with prose. (1) `hidden` is comment-only, which is the entire reason an injected class="hidden" fires this gate and did not fire the weaker copy - if that stopped being true, arm B would be proving nothing and this names it. (2) The identity defined.size + commentOnly.length === loose.size, which is the structural claim the comment strip makes. (3) Every comment-only word really does appear inside a CSS comment, a positive determination that stops a broken loose rule from filling the set with real classes. round3_theUnionMaskedTheDefect.rootCause: The attached-ness diff ran against MARKUP_SOURCES, which is the UNION of the served documents and the bake source. src/shell-homes.mjs still emitted data-disposition, and the union was satisfied. The union is RIGHT for the class question - a class renamed in the template without a re-bake ships stale, which is precisely why the scan list is derived from sendFile plus the bake sources. It is WRONG for the attached question: attached-ness is a claim about the document the browser receives, and src/shell-homes.mjs is served to nobody. I inherited the population from the class gate without asking whether it answered my question.
round3_theUnionMaskedTheDefect.twoOfThreeArmsWereSafeOnlyByLuck: The planner's point, and it is the same shape as data-tab passing by luck one round earlier. Removing an id alone fired and removing a hidden alone fired - but only because the bake source emits zero ids and zero hidden elements today, which I had measured myself and treated as a fact rather than as an accident. The first id emitted from that template would have acquired the same blindness silently.
round3_theUnionMaskedTheDefect.decision: BOTH options, not the preferred one alone, and the reason is measured rather than thorough-for-its-own-sake. Option 2 (bake freshness) does close the masking indirectly: if the document and the generator cannot disagree, the union cannot mask anything. But it makes THIS gate's correctness depend on a DIFFERENT test continuing to pass, so weakening or deleting the freshness test would silently restore the blindness. Option 1 makes the attached-ness question structurally correct whatever the bake state, and it is what makes case A fire NAMING data-disposition rather than reporting a stale bake. Option 2 is still worth doing on its own merits: it closes a second hole nobody has covered. So option 1 is the fix and option 2 is a second fix, and neither is rowed out.

option2_bakeFreshness.theSecondHole: The translation-boundary investigation recorded it and nothing had covered it: scripts/bake-connections.mjs's output is never byte-asserted, so a class, an id or an attribute changed on either side and not re-baked ships stale and passes every test in the repo - in EITHER direction, a stale document against a fresh generator or a fresh document against a stale one.

One implementation, so there is nothing to diverge (DEV_PROCESS 2.4) - the same move as fold A. Asserting a region comparison in the test instead would have been a second copy of the bake's region boundaries, which is the CTRL-1 shape this session has been removing all round.
option2_bakeFreshness.assertion: web/index.html is a FIXED POINT of the bake: baking the shipped document again changes nothing. That form covers the register rows and the connections-sources label together, because both are what the bake writes, and it needs nobody to remember to run anything. CRLF-normalized on both sides: the bake's region sentinels are literal newlines, so a raw comparison would fail on a Windows checkout while CI stayed green, which is a disagreement this repo has paid for before.
